setspec.lessonname: Optimized Drill Practice of Hiragana and Katakana

unit.unitinstructions:
Demographic Survey

Please answer the following 5 quick demographic questions, which may be useful for us to understand the data we collect.

あ Hiragana and Katakana

This lesson practices 92 Japanese kana, covering the hiragana and katakana symbols that appear constantly in beginner reading.

  • What you will do: Each card shows one character, and you type its romanized pronunciation from memory.
  • Timing: Study screens last about 16 seconds, drill screens about 8 seconds, review screens about 5 seconds, and correct confirmations last about 0.75 seconds.
  • How it works: Immediate feedback helps connect each visual form to its sound, and audio feedback can reinforce the answer aloud.
  • Why it helps: Adaptive scheduling brings confusing symbols back sooner and spaces out the ones you already know, supporting reading fluency before vocabulary and grammar work.

Watch for look-alike characters and script differences, then begin when you are ready.
